stories.title: September CPI surprised hotter; policy impact is unresolved without same‑session repricing.
stories.whatChanged: Headline and core CPI prints came in materially above prior monthly readings.
stories.whyItMatters: A materially hotter CPI print would normally reprice short‑end policy expectations and lift nominal yields if markets follow through.
stories.mechanism: Higher inflation raises expected policy path; futures/2Y moves and sustained long‑end adjustments are required to confirm market repricing.
stories.conclusion: CPI is hotter (observed), but canonical same‑session futures/2Y repricing to prove a policy‑path change is missing.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Observed Fed‑funds‑futures and intraday 2Y moves consistent with the CPI surprise within 24–48h.

stories.title: AI/semiconductor breadth remains supportive even as some semis show short‑term weakness.
stories.whatChanged: AI infrastructure breadth metrics remain elevated while a pocket of semiconductor names has pulled back over several sessions.
stories.whyItMatters: Concentrated AI/semis leadership can sustain indices even if rates rise, masking broader transmission into credit or volatility.
stories.mechanism: Strong AI fundamentals and concentrated cap flows support breadth; sector‑specific disappointment would expose broader sensitivity to rates.
stories.conclusion: AI/infra breadth is supportive and can sustain indices, but pockets of semis weakness increase downside vulnerability.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Sustained breadth deterioration ex‑AI or correlated credit/volatility widening.

stories.title: Real yields and a governed ACM term premium remain elevated; long‑end pressure is present but transmission is unresolved.
stories.whatChanged: 10Y and 30Y real yields are higher versus early October and the NY Fed ACM term‑premium is observable.
stories.whyItMatters: Elevated real yields and term‑premium dynamics can keep nominal yields high, affecting financing costs and sensitive sectors.
stories.mechanism: Higher real yields push nominal yields unless offset by breakeven/term‑premium moves; auction absorption and dealer positions mediate transmission to credit.
stories.conclusion: Long‑end real yields and an observed ACM term premium are present, but MOVE/auction sequencing to prove broad transmission is missing.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical MOVE series, intraday UST bar decomposition, or persistent auction tails/when‑issued evidence showing weak absorption.

investigations.question: Is repricing in long yields transmitting into credit spreads, volatility and breadth?
investigations.whyItMatters: If higher yields are broadening into credit and volatility, the regime shifts from idiosyncratic tech leadership to broad tightening risk.
investigations.currentExplanation: ACM term‑premium and nominal 10Y evidence exist, but canonical MOVE/Treasury‑volatility and clear HY/IG widening coincident with persistent yields are missing, so transmission remains unresolved.
investigations.expectedReaction: Conventional: rising real yields/front end should widen credit spreads, lift VIX and weaken broad breadth/small caps.
competingExplanations: AI/semiconductor concentration is masking broader weakness.
Credit widening is lagged and requires persistent yields.

candidateExplanations.discriminatingTest: Persistent when‑issued tails or weaker auction absorption and dealer position deterioration across next scheduled auctions.

investigations.invalidationCondition: Credit spreads and MOVE remain contained while nominal yields persistently rise without breadth deterioration.

verified.title: Long-end Treasury stress
verified.detail: On 24 September 2026, the U.S. Treasury par yield curve closed with the 10-year yield at 5.18% and the 30-year yield at 5.47%, confirming severe long-duration rate pressure.

verified.title: S&P concentration remains extreme
verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.title: Saudi/Houthi energy risk persists
verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: Natural-gas storage tightened
verified.detail: EIA reported Lower-48 working gas at 3,351 Bcf for the week ended 18 September 2026, a 53 Bcf weekly injection and 95 Bcf above the five-year average.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
